notes: The production inbox page size is 100. The accepted run created 101 uniquely keyed group threads through quata_chat_start_thread using two approved authenticated profiles, then read quata_chat_get_inbox_page with p_limit 100 and its returned three-field keyset cursor.

The first and second backend pages contained every one of the 101 owned fixture threads exactly once. Existing actor conversations were allowed on the second page, so the proof validates the real production boundary without deleting or reshaping pre-existing inbox data.

The runner acquired cleanup custody from the actor identity, exact unique-key set and QADATA subject prefix. It deleted 101 discovered owned threads inside one transaction, verified zero rows in all thread-owned tables and revoked both sessions.

The committed report contains only hashes, cardinalities, timestamps and named semantic steps. Credentials, tokens, database connection material, profile identifiers, thread identifiers, unique keys and absolute host paths are absent.

This evidence closes the previously explicit lack of deep pagination against the real backend. Platform accumulation, deduplication, hasMore termination and retry behavior remain covered by the existing common and platform pagination contracts; their runtime did not change, so their matrices were not repeated solely for this backend-evidence unit.
Forced network-loss recovery is a separate Conversations unit and is not claimed by this attestation.
